title: WorldTree: Towards 4D Dynamic Worlds from Monocular Video using Tree-Chains
claim: Prior methods optimize over the whole interval with coupled, amorphous composition; ours decomposes hierarchically in time and space via ancestral structure.
layout: 2 panels split by dashed line, 2 rows each, check/question-mark marks
description: A vertical dashed line splits the figure into 'Existing Methods' on the left and 'WorldTree' on the right, which has a purple tree logo. Row labels on the far left read 'Optimization Strategy' and 'Dynamic Representation'. The top row shows chains of circular nodes. On the left, one blue chain on the entire interval feeds two more chains through arrows, labeled 'Varying Deformation Patterns' with a dark question mark. On the right, a blue chain splits into orange sub-chains, then into short purple chains, labeled 'Temporal Partition Tree' with a green check. The bottom row has the left side showing global fusion and a fan of lines through a 'Local-wise Interference' box, marked with a question mark. The right side shows unions of colored chain segments and dashed ancestral links, labeled 'Spatial Ancestral Chains' with a green check. Blue, orange and purple carry the hierarchy levels.
caption: Intuitive illustration of WorldTree.
abstract: Dynamic reconstruction has achieved remarkable progress, but there remain challenges in monocular input for more practical applications. The prevailing works attempt to construct efficient motion representations, but lack a unified spatiotemporal decomposition framework, suffering from either holistic temporal optimization or coupled hierarchical spatial composition. To this end, we propose WorldTree, a unified framework comprising Temporal Partition Tree (TPT) that enables coarse-to-fine optimization based on the inheritance-based partition tree structure for hierarchical temporal decomposition, and Spatial Ancestral Chains (SAC) that recursively query ancestral hierarchical structure to provide complementary spatial dynamics while specializing motion representations across ancestral nodes. Experimental results on different datasets indicate that our proposed method achieves 8.26% improvement of LPIPS on NVIDIA-LS and 9.09% improvement of mLPIPS on DyCheck compared to the second-best method. Code: https://github.com/iCVTEAM/WorldTree.
